title: Fished to the Edge: Severe Overfishing Threatens Fish Stocks in Tanzania's Saline Rift Valley Lakes
content:
ABSTRACT

The Saline Rift Valley Lakes (SRVLs) of Tanzania support important inland fisheries, but increasing fishing pressure threatens their sustainability. This study assessed the status of fish stocks in two Tanzanian SRVLs: Lakes Kitangiri and Singida. Data on catches, species composition, catch per unit effort, maturity stages, and length-based indicators were collected from May to September 2023. Results indicate strong evidence of overfishing, reflected in declining catches and high exploitation rates. The endemic Oreochromis amphimelas (Manyara tilapia) was the most affected species, with exploitation rates (> 0.9) and fishing mortality 13-18 times above sustainable reference points. Length-frequency data showed that most individuals were captured before reaching optimal size. All sampled O. amphimelas exhibited small body depths relative to the legal 7.62 cm gill-net mesh size, and a high proportion of individuals were immature or early maturing. Interviews revealed widespread use of small-mesh nets, contributing to the capture of undersized fish. However, some individuals matured at relatively small sizes, suggesting possible shifts in population structure linked to environmental stressors. These findings reveal a mismatch between current mesh size regulations and the biological characteristics of target species. Revising gear regulations and adopting species-specific management measures are recommended to improve fisheries sustainability in SRVL.
